newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Rate on Yugo central bank bonds up at 121.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Rate on Yugo central bank bonds up at 121.8 pct.

text.p: The Yugoslav central bank raised the interest rate on its short-term bonds auctioned on Monday to an annual 121.8 percent, the Belgrade bourse said.
This compares to 77.9 percent rate set for the previous tranche of bonds auctioned on December 6.
The lowest rate ever on those securities, first launched in November 1995, stood at 60.7 percent while the highest was 128.29 percent.
The National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) offered at today's auction a new 45 million dinar tranche of 30-day bonds, but sold only 1 million dinars worth, the bourse said.
Buyer interest was low due to tight liquidity of the banking sector and long New Year and Christmas holidays, with banks reopening on January 8.
"Low sale at the auction causes no alarm. Our experience says it does not neccessarily indicate failure of an issue," a central bank official who asked not to be named told Reuters.
Analysts said NBY was clearly attempting to attract more investors with higher interest rate.
Sources close to the central bank said NBY was well aware the only investors were those who could obtain cheaper funds and reinvest in those securities.

Otherwise, they turn to the unofficial interbank dinar market, where funds fetch well over 400 percent a year, but also carry much greater risk, the source said. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
